original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Prove a three-factor upper bound for every two-role target over M_m(K), including all singular ranks, and give a literal constructor.
scope_change_reason: Self-contained algebraic side question from the right-vector alphabet lineage. It removes the invertible endpoint hypothesis of the semilocal theorem, rather than adding or pricing a native connector operation.
bottleneck_link: The formal alphabet separates base-field right vectors from algebra-valued coefficients. A universal factor bound closes its two-role full-matrix target problem; native implementation and the complete recursive invoice remain unknown.
stop_rule: Ship the first verified universal upper bound or record its obstruction; do not extend to more roles or other algebras.
evidence: PROOF.md proves cost<=3 for all fields and block sizes. verify.py checks the new constructor on all 65536 binary 4x4 targets, 3507 additional cases, 12 sharp witnesses and five controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Which simultaneous complement conditions suffice for singular targets over a product of full matrix algebras?
open_questions.why_it_matters: One common pair of free charts must work in every factor, unlike the single algebra here.
open_questions.first_step: Specify two binary M2 components whose preferred row or column swaps conflict, and test a common three-direction word.
open_questions.blocked_by: The componentwise maximal-rank chart choices in this proof need not coincide.

open_questions.question: Can one literal native producer and consumer implement these algebra-valued coefficients with a favorable complete invoice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Formal factor count does not provide a native supplier.
open_questions.first_step: State and price coefficient preparation, overwrite ownership, routing and restoration for one target.
open_questions.blocked_by: Native preparation, restoration, precision and stock costs remain unknown.
